panels.rationale: Single continuous-wave Doppler echocardiographic display from a human patient (prior triage: real patient echo, keep). The spectral trace shows the textbook late-peaking dagger-shaped systolic envelope of dynamic LVOT obstruction, with on-screen peak velocity 5.55 m/s and peak gradient 123.15 mmHg, matching the caption and in-text Valsalva-provoked gradient of 123 mmHg. Disease attribution to hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy is directly supported by the caption manifestation and the article title ('Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy'). The small 2D color sector at top is an integral part of the same echo acquisition, not a separate panel, so the figure is not compound. No skin, ethnicity, or age information is stated. [raw subtype: obstructive]

The cavity reduction is not in the allowed vocabulary and is therefore listed as a proposed finding rather than an invented finding_key.

in_text_mentions: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) revealed preserved systolic function and concentric hypertrophy (septal thickness 13 mm) with markedly elevated LVOT gradients (Figure 1). Transesophageal echocardiography (TOE) demonstrated a hypertrophied anterolateral papillary muscle inserting directly into the aortomitral junction, forming a rigid subvalvular ridge and causing fixed LVOT obstruction (Figure 2), without the evidence of SAM. Peak gradients were 212 mmHg (mean 105 mmHg, Vmax 7.3 m/s)—(Figure 3). Mild central aortic regurgitation was also observed.

panels.figure_caption: Transthoracic echocardiogram A transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated severe left ventricular hypertrophy with thickened papillary muscles in the parasternal long (A, B), parasternal short (C, D), apical 4 chamber (E, F), and apical 3 chamber (G, H, I) views with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction and almost complete left ventricular cavity obliteration during systole. Impaired diastolic filling is present due to global left ventricular hypertrophy (not shown) along with abnormally turbulent flow in the left ventricular outflow tract during systole (J) due to septal hypertrophy without systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. Continuous wave Doppler revealed resting and provoked gradients of 36 and 73 mmHg, respectively, across the left ventricular outflow tract (K) in the absence of aortic stenosis, confirming hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. in_text_mentions: was elevated at 392 pg/mL. The echocardiogram revealed severe concentric LHV, showcasing an interventricular septal diameter measuring 2.2 cm, a left ventricular posterior wall thickness of 1.9 cm, and a relative wall thickness of 0.94. Following a suggestion, a 2D echocardiogram was performed, revealing indications of asymmetrical septal hypertrophy and a peak gradient in the LVOT measuring 96 mmHg, suggestive of HOCM (Figure 1). According to the mother's account, the child was asymptomatic eight days prior before developing a fever of insidious onset that persisted despite medication. No complaints of loose stools or distress were reported.

findings.evidence: significant left ventricular hypertrophy with systolic anterior motion of the anterior mitral leaflet (caption)

panels.rationale: Real patient transesophageal echocardiogram from a case report of infective endocarditis complicating HOCM. The image and caption visibly demonstrate HOCM-specific features: significant left ventricular hypertrophy, systolic anterior motion of the anterior mitral leaflet, and a moderate eccentric posterior (SAM-related) mitral regurgitation jet, matching configured HOCM findings. The mitral valve vegetation (red arrow) is a complication of infective endocarditis, not an HOCM manifestation, so it is listed only as a proposed finding. Single-panel image, no copyright restriction, good image quality.

findings.label: Interstitial and perimysial myocardial fibrosis
findings.evidence: focal fibrous scar formation (asterisk in c)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: HE-stained endomyocardial biopsy from a patient with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy showing cardiomyocyte hypertrophy with vacuolar degeneration and aberrantly oriented myocytes (myofiber disarray), classic histologic features of HOCM. B: HE-stained endomyocardial biopsy from a patient with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy showing abnormal small vessels with thickened walls, consistent with intramural coronary arteriolar dysplasia, a classic histologic feature of HOCM. C: Masson's trichrome-stained endomyocardial biopsy from a patient with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy showing focal fibrous scar formation, representing replacement fibrosis, a recognized histologic feature of HOCM. D: Masson's trichrome-stained endomyocardial biopsy from a patient with hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy showing interstitial fibrosis and aberrantly oriented myocytes, both classic histologic features of HOCM.

panels.rationale: Single-panel parasternal short-axis echocardiogram from a real patient with HOCM. The caption and in-text explicitly describe the 'lip-nevus sign' (mitral leaflets as opposing 'lips' with a hypertrophied anterolateral papillary muscle as a central 'nevus'), a recently described marker of anomalous papillary muscle insertion, which is a recognized HOCM-associated finding present in the vocabulary. The image carries an arrow and an ellipse annotation. The lip-nevus sign itself is not in the allowed vocabulary and is therefore listed as a proposed finding. Disease attribution is strong given the HOCM-focused article title and the specific captioned manifestation. [raw subtype: anomalous_papillary_muscle_insertion]

The left atrium was dilated (left atrial volume index—LAVi 55 cm3/m2) with moderate mitral regurgitation. Whole exome sequencing did not reveal any gene associated with the disease. Biopsy and laboratory tests excluded common storage diseases.

plate_findings.evidence: in-text: 'asymmetrically hypertrophic myocardium under the aortic valve'; visual: thickened subaortic myocardium surrounding the closed aortic valve

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Cine cardiac MRI of a real patient showing the closed aortic valve with three leaflets; the surrounding subaortic myocardium is asymmetrically hypertrophied, consistent with HOCM. Disease attribution is supported by the article title and the in-text description of asymmetrically hypertrophic myocardium under the aortic valve. B: Cine cardiac MRI showing restricted aortic valve opening with blood flow passing only through the noncoronary leaflet during LV contraction, reflecting dynamic LVOT obstruction from hypertrophic myocardium. Real patient image of HOCM. C: Cine cardiac MRI showing the high-velocity blood flow region (arrow) from the LV through the noncoronary aortic leaflet, demonstrating dynamic LVOT obstruction in HOCM. Real patient image.

in_text_mentions: The Doppler-echocardiogram showed a combination of asymmetric septal and mid-ventricular HCM (Figure 2), and the anterobasal septum measured 21 mm. There was systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve with a subaortic gradient of 65 mm Hg (Figure 3), anteromedial septal thickness was 19 mm, there was a mid-ventricular systolic gradient of 20 mm Hg and an apical aneurysm. Ejection fraction was 55%. The presence of a restrictive mitral flow indicated an increase in left ventricle end-diastolic pressure due to diastolic dysfunction.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real frontal chest radiograph from the HOCM case; the enlarged cardiac silhouette with pulmonary vascular congestion is supported by the caption and in-text decompensated heart failure context as a HOCM-related radiographic manifestation. No diagnostic annotations beyond the panel letter. B: Real right anterior oblique chest radiograph in the same HOCM patient; it shows an enlarged cardiac silhouette with congestion and documents a left-sided dual-chamber ICD plus median sternotomy wires from prior septal myectomy, which is a recognized post-treatment HOCM radiographic appearance. No diagnostic annotations beyond the panel letter.

Electrocardiogram revealed junctional bradycardia, left ventricle (LV) hypertrophy, and no acute ischaemic changes (Figure 1).
